title: Known follow-ups
description: Items deliberately accepted rather than fixed, each verified still live in the current tree. None is a correctness defect in shipped behaviour.

title: workspaceAt collapses every stat failure into ErrNoWorkspace
description: internal/beads/workspace.go:67 discards the underlying os.Stat error, so an unreadable directory (EACCES) is reported identically to one that does not exist. The walk-failure message also says 'at or above the working directory' without naming the directory it started from, which matters more now that errors surface in the status bar.

title: Watcher.Close never closes the events channel
description: internal/watch/watch.go closes w.done and the fsnotify watcher but not w.events, so a consumer ranging over Events() blocks forever after Close returns. Harmless while Close only runs from run()'s deferred cleanup immediately before exit — the code says so — but it becomes a real goroutine leak the first time a watcher is restarted, for workspace switching or a daemon mode.

title: The --version test cannot fail for its stated reason
description: cmd/bv/main_test.go:29 asserts only that --version printed something non-empty, so it would pass on unrelated output. Assert the output names the version. Partially covered downstream by the release check that the published binary does not print 'dev'.

title: Adding a fourth view touches three places, not one
description: internal/tui/app.go spreads view registration across viewCount, the views array literal in NewModel, and viewKinds. Mechanical and textually obvious, but short of a single registration point. Worth collapsing only if a fourth view is actually added.

title: The coverage floor is written in two places with nothing checking they agree
description: MIN_COVERAGE appears in .github/workflows/ci.yml's coverage gate and in Taskfile.yml's coverage target. Both carry a comment saying they must move together, which is weaker than a test. internal/licensing already parses the workflows for other invariants, so asserting equality there is cheap.

title: RELEASING.md still describes the history re-initialisation as upcoming
description: docs/RELEASING.md Step 1 instructs the publisher to re-initialise history and tag. Once that has happened, trim Step 1.1 to a sentence so a later release does not read instructions for something already behind it.

title: ARCHITECTURE.md explains the reload design but carries no measurements
description: The full-reload-on-every-write design is justified there in prose. The numbers that justify it — decode time, per-keystroke latency and the point at which reload cost starts to show — live only in README.md's Scale section. A pointer, or the figures themselves, belongs beside the reasoning.

title: Counts derives blockedness twice for every open issue
description: Snapshot.Counts calls IsBlocked, then IsReady, which calls IsBlocked again. Measured at 0.4 ms per frame for 10,000 issues, so this is not worth doing for speed — only if the duplication itself becomes a correctness hazard.

title: bv hangs instead of reporting when stdin is not a terminal
description: Run from a shell with a controlling terminal but with stdin redirected — 'echo | bv', 'bv < /dev/null' — bubbletea falls back to opening /dev/tty and blocks there forever, before rendering anything and with no message. The user sees a hang, not an error. Found via cmd/bv's own test, which now sidesteps it with Setsid; that fixes the test, not the behaviour. A terminal check at startup that exits with a clear message would be the fix.

design:
# Framed panes, pane focus and live filtering

Six interface changes to `bv`, batched because they interlock: a frame around
each pane, a focus model that the frame indicates, a richer list row, a
full-screen board, a hide-closed toggle that means the same thing everywhere,
and a filter that applies as you type.

Today every pane is borderless and separated by a single blank gutter column;
there is no notion of focus, so the detail pane can only ever be paged with
`pgup`/`pgdown`; list rows are styled as one flat unit with no date; the board
shares the terminal with a detail pane it has no room for; `c` narrows only the
tree; and the filter applies only on Enter.

## Global constraint

The non-test Go budget stands at 6,299 lines against a cap of 6,300. Every
ticket here adds code. Whichever lands first raises the cap deliberately and
records the reasoning in its commit message, the same procedure the cap's
previous raise followed. Do not raise it silently, and do not spread the raise
across six commits.

The structural tripwires are not relaxed by that raise: `Model` stays capped at
12 fields, no non-test file exceeds 500 lines, no behavioural type exceeds 20
fields, and no file declares more than five exported types.

## Architecture

Nothing here changes the shape of the codebase. The root model still owns the
filter and applies it once for all three views; the views still sit behind the
`View` interface; the detail pane still displays whatever the active view has
selected rather than owning a cursor.

Three seams absorb almost all of the work:

- `tui.Compute` (`layout.go`) already takes a `showDetail` parameter and already
  clamps every dimension at zero. Borders and the full-screen board are both
  geometry changes expressed there.
- `tui.handleKey` (`keys.go`) already routes in a fixed order — overlay, then
  globals, then the active view. Focus is one more branch in that order, not a
  new dispatch mechanism.
- `beads.Filter` is already the single place a query is interpreted. Global
  hide-closed and live filtering are both changes to when `SetFilter` is
  called, not to what a filter means.

State that has nowhere else to live goes on `overlayState`, one of the two
structs sanctioned to grow instead of `Model`.

## Features

### T1 — Frame each pane with a border

Draw a border around the active view pane and the detail pane. `theme.Border`
exists already and no pane currently uses it.

A border costs two columns and two rows per pane. `Compute` must subtract them
before the result reaches `View.SetSize`, or every view renders two cells wider
than the frame around it. The border replaces `gutterWidth`'s blank column
rather than adding to it. Below the width at which two bordered panes fit, fall
back to unbordered rendering rather than clipping a frame.

Golden frames store the ANSI-stripped output, so box-drawing characters land in
the goldens. Regenerate them; do not exempt them.

Acceptance criteria:
- Side-by-side and stacked panes both render a border.
- `ListWidth`, `DetailWidth` and the pane heights handed to `SetSize` exclude
  the border, verified by a test that renders at a known size and measures the
  frame.
- A 0x0 terminal, and any width too narrow for two bordered panes, renders
  without panicking and without exceeding the terminal width.
- Goldens regenerated.

### T2 — Tab cycles focus between the view pane and the detail pane

Depends on T1: the border is the focus indicator.

Tab moves focus between the active view pane and the detail pane. The focused
pane's border renders in `theme.Accent`, the unfocused one in `theme.Border`.

With the detail pane focused, `up`/`down`/`k`/`j` scroll its viewport and the
active view's cursor does not move. `pgup`/`pgdown` keep scrolling the detail
pane regardless of focus, so the unconditional routing in `handleKey` becomes
conditional rather than disappearing.

The board's swimlane cycling moves off `tab` to `s`. Help and the status bar
follow. Tab is a no-op whenever no detail pane is on screen — which after T4 is
the whole board view.

`Model` is at its 12-field cap, so the focus flag rides on `overlayState`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Tab with the detail pane on screen moves focus; the rendered border colours
  swap.
- With detail focused, `j`/`k` scroll detail and leave the view's `SelectedID`
  unchanged; with the view focused, they move the cursor and leave the detail
  scroll offset unchanged.
- `s` cycles the board swimlane; `tab` no longer does.
- Tab with no detail pane on screen changes nothing.
- Help lists the new bindings and `internal/tui/help_test.go` still agrees with
  the board's `HelpKeys`.

### T3 — Colour and date the list rows

Colour the type glyph per issue type and the status column per status, and add
a right-aligned relative `updated_at` column ("2d ago", at most six cells).
The date is dropped first when the pane is narrow — before labels, before the
title.

`listview.delegate.row` currently styles the whole row once, as a unit,
deliberately: a styled span in the middle of a row emits its own reset code,
which drops the outer style for everything after it. Per-column colour means
composing pre-styled segments instead, and deciding what a selected row does —
the selection background has to survive across every segment boundary, or a
selected row will show gaps.

Needs two theme methods alongside the existing `TypeGlyph` and `Priority`: one
mapping an issue type to a style, one mapping a status to a style. Both degrade
under `SchemeAgnostic`, which has no hex palette and must stay legible on a
background it knows nothing about.

Acceptance criteria:
- The type glyph and the status column each render in a type- and
  status-specific style.
- Every row carries a relative updated column, right-aligned, absent when the
  pane cannot afford it.
- A selected row renders differently from an unselected one, with no style gap
  across segment boundaries — asserted separately from the content golden.
- Under `SchemeAgnostic` no colour is emitted that assumes a background.
- Column alignment survives an overlong custom status, as `statusColumnWidth`'s
  comment already requires.

### T4 — Board runs full screen; Enter opens the item in the list

`applyLayout` hardcodes `Compute`'s `showDetail` to `true`. Passing
`m.active != boardSlot` instead gives the board the full body width and height:
no detail pane, no gutter, no second border.

Enter on a card switches the active view to the list and selects the card's
issue there. Both `SelectByID` methods already exist. A failed lookup leaves
the view switch alone rather than jumping to an unrelated row.

Acceptance criteria:
- With the board active, the board's `SetSize` receives the full body width;
  the detail pane is not rendered.
- Switching away from the board restores the two-pane layout without a resize
  event.
- Enter on a card makes the list active with that issue selected.
- Enter on an empty column, where `Selected()` is nil, does nothing.

### T5 — `c` becomes a global hide-closed toggle

Promote `c` from the tree to `Model.filter.HideClosed`, applied once in the
root and handed to all three views — the contract `Filter`'s own doc comment
states. `treeview`'s local `hideClosed` field, its `Retain` call and
`State.HideClosed` all retire.

The persisted `hide_closed` in existing tree state files is dropped, not
migrated into the global filter at startup. Restoring a tree-local narrowing as
a workspace-wide one would silently hide closed issues in two panes the user
never set it on. `--hide-closed` and the config file stay the only startup
sources. Old state files keep loading: an extra JSON field is ignored.

Acceptance criteria:
- `c` toggles hide-closed from any view, and all three views narrow together.
- The status bar reflects it via `Filter.Describe`, which already handles it.
- Help drops the "(tree)" qualifier.
- A state file written before this change still loads, and its `hide_closed`
  value does not reach the filter.
- Tree expansion and selection still persist and restore.

### T6 — Filter applies live, debounced

Each keystroke in the filter overlay schedules a re-apply roughly 150 ms out
via `tea.Tick`, carrying a token so a stale tick cannot apply a buffer two
keystrokes old — the token pattern `clearStatusMsg` already uses for yank
confirmations. Enter still commits and closes the overlay. The empty-filter
screen updates live along with everything else.

Escape currently discards an edit that was never applied. Once typing applies
as it goes, Escape has to restore: `overlayState` remembers the filter text as
it was when the overlay opened, and Escape puts it back and re-applies.

Acceptance criteria:
- Typing into the overlay narrows the views without Enter, after the delay.
- A tick carrying a stale token applies nothing.
- Escape restores the filter exactly as it was when the overlay opened,
  including the case where the overlay was opened on an already-active filter.
- Enter still commits and closes the overlay.
- The delay is a named constant, not a literal at its use site.

## Testing

Every package keeps its single `Test<Package>` entry point wiring suites, with
all assertions as suite methods. Golden view tests store ANSI-stripped frames
and assert styling separately — T1 and T3 both change what those goldens hold,
so both regenerate rather than exempt.

## Out of scope

Writing anywhere inside `.beads/`, spawning a subprocess, and validating
`status` or `issue_type` values all remain out of scope; `bv` renders what it
is given. No new direct dependency is needed for any of these six.

notes:
# Global Constraints

Every task below implicitly includes this section. Values are copied verbatim
from CLAUDE.md and `.golangci.yml`; do not restate them per task, and do not
relax one to make a task fit.

## The gate

- `task check` runs `format:check` → `lint` → `test` and must exit 0 before
  every commit.
- Run it again **after** `git add`, not only before. The `internal/licensing`
  sweep enumerates git-tracked files, so a new file that is not yet staged is
  invisible to it: stage first, then run the gate, then commit.
- Never pass `--no-verify`. Do not skip hooks.
- Do not run `git push` or `gh` in this repository — it has no remote.

## Size tripwires

- Non-test Go: at most **6,300 lines** total, and the tree stands at **6,299**.
  The first task to land raises the cap deliberately and records the reasoning
  in its own commit message. It is raised **once**, for the whole epic — not
  six times, and never silently.
- `cmd/bv/main.go`: at most 150 lines.
- No non-test source file exceeds 500 lines. Test files that map to exactly one
  `suite.Suite` are exempt from the line cap.
- No behavioural type has more than 20 fields. `beads.Issue` is exempt.
- At most 5 exported type declarations per file (`revive` `max-public-structs`).
- `tui.Model` is capped at 12 fields by `TestModelStaysSmall` and is **full**.
  New root state rides on `statusState` or `overlayState`, the two structs
  sanctioned to grow.
- Never add a `//nolint` that turns out to be unnecessary — `nolintlint` fails
  the build on an unused directive.

## Code style

- No package-level `var`, no `init()` (`gochecknoglobals` / `gochecknoinits`).
- `funcorder`: exported methods before unexported; constructors first.
- `revive` function-length: at most 40 statements / 60 lines (non-test).
- `gocyclo` / `cyclop`: cyclomatic complexity at most 10.
- `lll` / `golines`: 120 columns (non-test).
- `wrapcheck`: wrap every error crossing a package boundary,
  e.g. `fmt.Errorf("decode issues.jsonl: %w", err)`.
- `ireturn`: return concrete types, not interfaces. Accepting interfaces is fine.
- `sloglint`: `no-global: all`, lowercased messages, snake_case keys.
- `godot`: comments end with a period.
- Formatters: `gofumpt`, `gci` (sections: standard, default,
  `prefix(github.com/Toshik1978/beads-viewer)`), `golines` at 120 columns.
- `revive`'s `flag-parameter` rule is **disabled** in this repository, so a
  `focused bool` parameter is allowed — `Compute(width, height int, showDetail
  bool)` already relies on that.
- Write comments that explain *why*, not what the code already says.

## Dependencies

- At most 9 direct dependencies. **No task here adds one.** Everything needed
  is already present: `charm.land/bubbletea/v2`, `charm.land/bubbles/v2`,
  `charm.land/lipgloss/v2`, `charm.land/glamour/v2`,
  `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi`, `github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify`,
  `github.com/spf13/cobra`, `github.com/goccy/go-yaml`,
  `github.com/stretchr/testify`.
- Only bubbletea, bubbles, lipgloss and glamour use the `charm.land` vanity
  path; the `x/` repositories stay at `github.com/charmbracelet/x/...`.

## Testing

- Exactly one top-level `func Test<Package>(t *testing.T)` per package, wiring
  suites only — `suite.Run(t, new(...))` calls and nothing else.
- Every assertion is a suite method (`s.Equal`, `s.Require().NoError`,
  `s.Contains`). Never a bare `func TestX(t *testing.T)` with `require.X(t, …)`.
- Table-driven subtests use `s.Run(tc.name, func() { … })`.
- Golden view tests store the **ANSI-stripped** frame (`ansi.Strip`).
  Regenerate with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./...`. Styling is asserted
  separately from content — at minimum that a selected row's rendering differs
  from an unselected one.

## Behavioural invariants

- `bv` is read-only with respect to `.beads/`: it never writes anywhere inside
  that directory and never spawns a subprocess. No package under this module
  other than `internal/licensing` may import `os/exec`.
- The write to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/bv/trees/` is outside `.beads/` and is expected
  — do not "fix" it by removing it.
- `bv` renders rather than validates: unknown `status` and `issue_type` values
  stay raw strings, unknown JSON fields are ignored, labels are never
  validated. A workspace `br` itself would reject must still open.

## Commits

- Conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `test:`, `chore:`, `docs:`,
  `refactor:`.
- **No `Co-Authored-By`, no `Claude-Session`, no AI-attribution trailer of any
  kind.** Subject and body only.
- Feature branches use the `feature/` prefix — never `feat/` or `feat-`.

## Licensing

- Never name another project, or anyone else's filesystem path, in any
  git-tracked file. This applies to code, comments, commit messages and test
  fixtures alike.

title: Route navigation keys to whichever pane holds focus
description: While the detail pane holds focus it takes every key the global bindings did not consume; pgup/pgdown reach it either way. Consumes: overlay.focus, focusView, focusDetail, detailOnScreen from the focus task. Produces: no new identifiers — handleKey's fall-through changes shape only.
design:
### Task 2.2: Route navigation keys to whichever pane holds focus

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/tui/keys.go` (`handleKey`'s tail)
- Test: `internal/tui/app_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes, from Task 2.1: `m.overlay.focus`, `focusView`, `focusDetail`,
  `m.detailOnScreen()`.
- Produces: no new identifiers. `handleKey`'s fall-through changes shape only.

The rule: **while the detail pane holds focus, every key the global bindings
did not consume goes to the detail pane** — not a hand-picked subset. A focus
model that forwards only `up`/`down` leaves `g`, `home` and the rest silently
moving a cursor the user cannot see. `pgup`/`pgdown` keep reaching the detail
pane regardless of focus, which is what they were bound for.

`bubbles/v2/viewport`'s own `KeyMap` already binds `up`/`k`, `down`/`j`,
`pgup`/`pgdown` and the half-page keys, so forwarding is all that is needed —
do not add a second keymap here.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

Append to `appTestSuite` in `internal/tui/app_test.go`. The fixture needs one
issue with a description long enough to overflow the pane, or nothing will
scroll:

```go
// longIssue is an issue whose description cannot fit a 40-row detail pane, so
// scrolling it actually changes what is rendered.
func longIssue() beads.Issue {
	body := strings.Repeat("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. ", 200)

	return beads.Issue{
		ID:          "bv-1",
		Title:       "long",
		Status:      beads.StatusOpen,
		Description: body,
	}
}

func (s *appTestSuite) TestFocusedDetailPaneTakesTheNavigationKeys() {
	m := s.newModel([]beads.Issue{longIssue(), {ID: "bv-2", Title: "second", Status: beads.StatusOpen}})
	m.Update(tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: 120, Height: 40})
	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: tea.KeyTab})

	selected := m.SelectedID()
	before := ansi.Strip(m.View())
	for range 5 {
		m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: 'j', Text: "j"})
	}

	s.Equal(selected, m.SelectedID(),
		"the view's cursor must not move while the detail pane holds focus")
	s.NotEqual(before, ansi.Strip(m.View()), "the detail pane must have scrolled")
}

func (s *appTestSuite) TestUnfocusedDetailPaneLeavesTheKeysToTheView() {
	m := s.newModel([]beads.Issue{longIssue(), {ID: "bv-2", Title: "second", Status: beads.StatusOpen}})
	m.Update(tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: 120, Height: 40})

	s.Equal("bv-1", m.SelectedID())
	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: 'j', Text: "j"})

	s.Equal("bv-2", m.SelectedID(),
		"with the view focused, j moves the view's own cursor")
}

	m := s.newModel([]beads.Issue{longIssue()})
	m.Update(tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: 120, Height: 40})

	// View focused — pgdown is bound to the detail pane specifically.
	before := ansi.Strip(m.View())
	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: tea.KeyPgDown})

	s.NotEqual(before, ansi.Strip(m.View()))
}
```

title: Type and status styles on the theme
description: Two theme methods mapping issue types and statuses onto styles the palette already carries, so both hue schemes stay tuned and SchemeAgnostic keeps assuming nothing about the background. Consumes: nothing. Produces: theme.Theme.Type(k beads.IssueType) lipgloss.Style and theme.Theme.Status(s beads.Status) lipgloss.Style.
design:
### Task 3.1: Type and status styles on the theme

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/tui/theme/theme.go`
- Test: `internal/tui/theme/theme_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing.
- Produces:
  - `func (t theme.Theme) Type(k beads.IssueType) lipgloss.Style`
  - `func (t theme.Theme) Status(s beads.Status) lipgloss.Style`

Task 3.3 is the only caller.

**The design decision, made here so 3.3 does not have to:** both methods map
known values onto the styles the palette *already* carries — `Error`,
`Accent`, `Title`, `Muted`, `Base` — rather than adding new colours to
`palette`. Three reasons, all of which the alternative fails:

1. Those styles are already tuned per scheme, so a light terminal gets a
   readable variant for free.
2. `SchemeAgnostic` gets correct behaviour with no extra work: it builds
   `Muted` from `Faint(true)` and `Base` from no attributes at all, precisely
   because it must assume nothing about the background. A new hex entry in
   `palette` would have to solve that problem again, and `agnosticPalette`'s
   own doc comment explains why it deliberately leaves those slots unset.
3. It adds no field to `palette`, which is under the same 20-field cap as any
   other type.

Both enums are **open** — `IssueType` and `Status` are strings, and
`internal/beads` keeps unknown values verbatim on purpose. The `default` arm
is therefore load-bearing, not defensive: it is the path a custom status from
a real workspace takes.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

Append to `internal/tui/theme/theme_test.go`'s existing suite:

```go
func (s *themeTestSuite) TestTypeStylesDistinguishTheCommonTypes() {
	th := theme.New(config.ThemeDark, theme.BackgroundDark)

	bug := th.Type(beads.TypeBug).Render("x")
	epic := th.Type(beads.TypeEpic).Render("x")
	task := th.Type(beads.TypeTask).Render("x")

	s.NotEqual(bug, epic)
	s.NotEqual(bug, task)
	s.NotEqual(epic, task)
}

func (s *themeTestSuite) TestUnknownTypeFallsBackToBase() {
	th := theme.New(config.ThemeDark, theme.BackgroundDark)

	// br models issue_type as an open set and bv renders rather than
	// validates, so a type nobody here has heard of must still get a style.
	s.Equal(th.Base.Render("x"), th.Type(beads.IssueType("wibble")).Render("x"))
}

func (s *themeTestSuite) TestStatusStylesDistinguishProgressFromBlocked() {
	th := theme.New(config.ThemeDark, theme.BackgroundDark)

	s.NotEqual(
		th.Status(beads.StatusInProgress).Render("x"),
		th.Status(beads.StatusBlocked).Render("x"),
	)
	s.NotEqual(
		th.Status(beads.StatusOpen).Render("x"),
		th.Status(beads.StatusClosed).Render("x"),
	)
}

func (s *themeTestSuite) TestUnknownStatusFallsBackToBase() {
	th := theme.New(config.ThemeDark, theme.BackgroundDark)

	s.Equal(th.Base.Render("x"), th.Status(beads.Status("triaging")).Render("x"))
}

func (s *themeTestSuite) TestTypeAndStatusStayBackgroundAgnostic() {
	th := theme.New(config.ThemeAuto, theme.BackgroundUnknown)
	s.Require().Equal(theme.SchemeAgnostic, th.Scheme)

	// Base sets no attributes at all under this scheme — that is the one pair
	// guaranteed legible when nothing about the background is known — so the
	// fallback must not have acquired a colour on the way through.
	s.Equal("x", th.Type(beads.IssueType("wibble")).Render("x"))
	s.Equal("x", th.Status(beads.Status("triaging")).Render("x"))
	s.NotEqual(th.Status(beads.StatusOpen).Render("x"), th.Status(beads.StatusBlocked).Render("x"))
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run them to verify they fail**

Run: `go test ./internal/tui/theme/ -run TestTheme`

Expected: compile error — `th.Type` and `th.Status` undefined.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement both methods**

In `internal/tui/theme/theme.go`, beside `Priority` and `TypeGlyph` (exported
methods stay together, before the unexported helpers — `funcorder`):

```go
// Type returns the style an issue type's glyph is rendered in.
//
// Every arm reuses a style the palette already carries rather than
// introducing a colour of its own: those are already tuned per scheme, and
// SchemeAgnostic builds Muted and Base from attributes rather than colours
// precisely because it must assume nothing about the background.
//
// The default arm is the open-enum path, not a defensive one — br models
// issue_type as an open set and bv renders rather than validates, so an
// unrecognised type is data, not an error.
func (t Theme) Type(k beads.IssueType) lipgloss.Style {
	switch k {
	case beads.TypeBug:
		return t.Error
	case beads.TypeEpic:
		return t.Title
	case beads.TypeFeature, beads.TypeQuestion:
		return t.Accent
	case beads.TypeChore, beads.TypeDocs:
		return t.Muted
	case beads.TypeTask:
		return t.Base
	default:
		return t.Base
	}
}

// Status returns the style a status label is rendered in. See Type for why
// these reuse existing styles and why the default arm carries real traffic.
func (t Theme) Status(s beads.Status) lipgloss.Style {
	switch s {
	case beads.StatusInProgress:
		return t.Accent
	case beads.StatusBlocked:
		return t.Error
	case beads.StatusPinned:
		return t.Title
	case beads.StatusClosed, beads.StatusTombstone, beads.StatusDeferred, beads.StatusDraft:
		return t.Muted
	case beads.StatusOpen:
		return t.Base
	default:
		return t.Base
	}
}
```

`TypeTask` and `StatusOpen` are named explicitly rather than folded into
`default` so that adding a type or status to `internal/beads` shows up as an
unhandled case to a reader, not as a silent fall-through.

Run: `go test ./internal/tui/theme/ -run TestTheme`

Expected: PASS.

```bash

task check
git commit -m "feat(theme): style issue types and statuses

Type and Status map the known values onto styles the palette already
carries, so both schemes stay tuned and SchemeAgnostic keeps assuming
nothing about the background. Both enums are open, so the default arm is
the path a custom value from a real workspace takes."
```

design:
### Task 4.1: Give the board the whole body

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/tui/app.go` (`applyLayout`)
- Modify: `internal/tui/keys.go` (`handleViewSwitchKey` — see Step 4)
- Test: `internal/tui/internal_test.go` (`WhiteBoxSuite`)
- Test: `internal/tui/app_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes, from Task 2.1: `handleViewSwitchKey`, `m.overlay.focus`.
- Produces: `func (m *Model) showsDetail() bool` — whether the current active
  view gets a detail pane beside it. `applyLayout` passes it to `Compute`.

**The trap in this task.** `applyLayout` currently runs only on
`tea.WindowSizeMsg`. Once the layout depends on which view is active, a view
switch has to recompute it too — otherwise pressing `3` gives you a board
still sized for a two-pane split, and it stays that way until the terminal is
resized. Step 4 is not optional.

Append to `WhiteBoxSuite` in `internal/tui/internal_test.go`, which already
has `spyView` for exactly this kind of assertion:

### Task 5: Promote hide-closed from the tree to a global filter

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/tui/keys.go` (`KeyMap`, `DefaultKeyMap`, `handleActionKey`)
- Modify: `internal/tui/status.go` (delete `treeHiddenCount`)
- Modify: `internal/tui/app.go` (`statusLine`)

- Modify: `internal/tui/treeview/nav.go` (delete `ToggleHideClosed`,
  `HiddenCount`, the `hideClosed` field and the `c` binding)
- Modify: `internal/tui/treeview/render.go` (the `hideClosed` field on the
  render struct — read it and remove what becomes dead)
- Modify: `internal/tui/treeview/state.go` (`State.HideClosed`)
- Test: `internal/tui/app_test.go`, `internal/tui/treeview/state_test.go`,
  `internal/tui/treeview/nav_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `handleActionKey` (Task 2.1); `beads.Filter.HideClosed` and
  `Model.SetFilter`, both already present.
- Produces:
  - `KeyMap.HideClosed key.Binding` bound to `c`.
  - `func (m *Model) toggleHideClosed()`
  - Removed: `treeview.Model.ToggleHideClosed`, `treeview.Model.HiddenCount`,
    `treeview.State.HideClosed`, `tui.Model.treeHiddenCount`.

**The consequence to understand before starting.** The tree does not filter
rows — it prunes structurally. `rebuild` calls `Retain(Build(snapshot),
Filter{HideClosed: …})`, and `Retain` keeps a non-matching *ancestor* when a
descendant matches, so today a closed epic stays on screen as scaffolding for
its open children.

Under a global filter the closed epic is gone from the snapshot before
`Build` ever sees it. Its open children are **not** lost: `indexHierarchy`
skips a parent-child edge whose parent is absent from the snapshot
(`snapshot.go:126`), so those children become roots. That is a real,
deliberate behaviour change — closed parents stop appearing as scaffolding
and their children re-root — and Step 1 pins it. Do not try to preserve the
old scaffolding; that is what "one filter, one meaning" costs, and the
re-rooting is already implemented and commented as the guard against silent
subtree loss.

`rebuild` must keep calling `Retain` with a **zero** filter. `Retain`'s doc
comment is explicit that a zero filter is not the identity — it still drops
tombstones — so deleting the call would put deletion markers on screen.

```go
// scaffolding; under a global filter it is gone and the child re-roots.
func closedParentIssues() []beads.Issue {
	return []beads.Issue{
		{ID: "bv-1", Title: "closed epic", IssueType: beads.TypeEpic, Status: beads.StatusClosed},
		{
			ID: "bv-2", Title: "open child", IssueType: beads.TypeTask, Status: beads.StatusOpen,
			Dependencies: []beads.Dependency{{DependsOnID: "bv-1", Type: beads.DepParentChild}},
```

title: Apply the filter as you type, debounced, and make Escape restore
description: Debounce a live filter apply on every keystroke with a generation token, and make Escape restore the filter as it was when the overlay opened. One task, not two: live filtering makes 'Escape discards the edit' meaningless, so splitting them would leave a red test at a commit boundary. Consumes: Model.SetFilter, overlay.buffer, overlay.kind, handleActionKey. Produces: filterDebounce const; filterTickMsg{token int}; overlayState.filterToken and overlayState.filterBefore; Model.scheduleFilterApply() tea.Cmd; Model.applyBufferedFilter(token int); Model.closeFilterOverlay(); Model.FilterForTest() in export_test.go.
design:
### Task 6: Apply the filter as you type, debounced, and make Escape restore

These two are one task, not two. Once typing applies as it goes, "Escape
discards the edit" stops being meaningful — `TestEscapeClosesTheFilterBoxAnd
DiscardsTheEdit` goes red the moment the debounce lands. Splitting them would
put a red test at a commit boundary, and the gate has to exit 0 before every
commit.

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/tui/keys.go` (`overlayState`, `handleActionKey`'s Filter
  case, `handleFilterKey`, plus the tick message and two new methods)
- Modify: `internal/tui/app.go` (`Update` — one new case)
- Test: `internal/tui/app_test.go`, `internal/tui/export_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `Model.SetFilter`, `m.overlay.buffer`, `m.overlay.kind`,
  `handleActionKey` (Task 2.1).
- Produces, all in package `tui`:
  - `const filterDebounce = 150 * time.Millisecond`
  - `type filterTickMsg struct{ token int }`
  - `overlayState.filterToken int` and `overlayState.filterBefore beads.Filter`
  - `func (m *Model) scheduleFilterApply() tea.Cmd`
  - `func (m *Model) applyBufferedFilter(token int)`
  - `func (m *Model) FilterForTest() beads.Filter` in `export_test.go`

**The bug to avoid, stated up front.** The tick closure must capture the token
**by value at schedule time**:

```go
	m.overlay.filterToken++
	token := m.overlay.filterToken           // capture the value…
	return tea.Tick(filterDebounce, func(time.Time) tea.Msg {
		return filterTickMsg{token: token}   // …not m.overlay.filterToken
	})
```

A closure reading `m.overlay.filterToken` when the tick *fires* always sees
the latest generation, so every stale tick reports itself as current and the
token does nothing. Get this wrong and the first test below still passes while
the debounce silently degrades to "apply every keystroke, out of order" — the
second test is the one that catches it.

`overlayState` reaches 8 fields with these two, well inside the 20-field cap.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

Add the seam to `internal/tui/export_test.go`, beside the others:

```go
// FilterForTest exposes the applied filter, so a test can tell "the buffer
// holds this text" apart from "the filter has actually been applied" — the
// distinction the whole debounce turns on.
func (m *Model) FilterForTest() beads.Filter { return m.filter }
```

Append to `appTestSuite` in `internal/tui/app_test.go`:

```go
func (s *appTestSuite) twoIssues() []beads.Issue {
	return []beads.Issue{
		{ID: "bv-1", Title: "alpha", Status: beads.StatusOpen},
		{ID: "bv-2", Title: "beta", Status: beads.StatusOpen},
	}
}

func (s *appTestSuite) TestTypingNarrowsTheViewsWithoutEnter() {
	m := s.newModel(s.twoIssues())
	m.Update(tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: 120, Height: 40})

	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: '/', Text: "/"})
	_, cmd := m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: 'a', Text: "a"})

	s.Require().NotNil(cmd, "a keystroke must schedule a debounced apply")
	// Run the scheduled command for the tick it would have delivered rather
	// than sleeping: tea.Tick's own timer is not this test's concern.
	m.Update(cmd())

	out := ansi.Strip(m.View())
	s.Contains(out, "bv-1", "alpha matches")
	s.NotContains(out, "bv-2", "beta does not")
}

func (s *appTestSuite) TestAStaleTickAppliesNothing() {
	m := s.newModel(s.twoIssues())
	m.Update(tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: 120, Height: 40})
	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: '/', Text: "/"})

	// Type "b", hold on to its tick, then type "e" — the first tick is now a
	// keystroke stale and must not narrow anything to "b" alone.
	_, stale := m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: 'b', Text: "b"})
	s.Require().NotNil(stale)
	staleMsg := stale()
	_, fresh := m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: 'e', Text: "e"})
	s.Require().NotNil(fresh)

	m.Update(staleMsg)
	s.Empty(m.FilterForTest().Text, "a stale tick must apply nothing at all")

	m.Update(fresh())
	s.Equal("be", m.FilterForTest().Text)
}

func (s *appTestSuite) TestEnterStillCommitsAndClosesTheOverlay() {
	m := s.newModel(s.twoIssues())
	m.Update(tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: 120, Height: 40})

	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: '/', Text: "/"})
	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: 'a', Text: "a"})
	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: tea.KeyEnter})

	s.Equal("a", m.FilterForTest().Text)
	s.NotContains(ansi.Strip(m.View()), "filter: ", "the overlay is closed")
}

func (s *appTestSuite) TestEscapeRestoresTheFilterAsItWasWhenTheOverlayOpened() {
	m := s.newModel(s.twoIssues())
	m.Update(tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: 120, Height: 40})

	// Open on an already-active filter — the case a plain "clear on escape"
	// gets wrong, and the reason this is a restore rather than a reset.
	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: '/', Text: "/"})
	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: 'a', Text: "a"})
	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: tea.KeyEnter})
	s.Require().Equal("a", m.FilterForTest().Text)

	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: '/', Text: "/"})
	_, cmd := m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: 'b', Text: "b"})
	m.Update(cmd())
	s.Require().Equal("ab", m.FilterForTest().Text, "typing applied live")

	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: tea.KeyEscape})

	s.Equal("a", m.FilterForTest().Text,
		"escape restores what was there, it does not clear")
	s.Contains(ansi.Strip(m.View()), "bv-1")
}

func (s *appTestSuite) TestATickArrivingAfterEscapeAppliesNothing() {
	m := s.newModel(s.twoIssues())
	m.Update(tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: 120, Height: 40})

	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: '/', Text: "/"})
	_, cmd := m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: 'b', Text: "b"})
	s.Require().NotNil(cmd)
	inFlight := cmd()

	m.Update(tea.KeyPressMsg{Code: tea.KeyEscape})
	m.Update(inFlight)

	s.Empty(m.FilterForTest().Text,
		"a tick that outlived the overlay must not re-narrow anything")
}
```

Replace `TestEscapeClosesTheFilterBoxAndDiscardsTheEdit` (`app_test.go:265`)
with `TestEscapeRestoresTheFilterAsItWasWhenTheOverlayOpened` above — it is
the same guarantee in the form that survives live filtering. Keep
`TestEscapeClearsANonMatchingFilterFromTheActiveView` (`app_test.go:286`)
untouched: that is the *closed*-overlay Escape, a different key path
(`handleActionKey`), and this task must not change it.

- [ ] **Step 2: Run them to verify they fail**

Run: `go test ./internal/tui/ -run TestTUI`

Expected: `TestTypingNarrowsTheViewsWithoutEnter` FAILs on
`s.Require().NotNil(cmd)` — `handleFilterKey` returns `nil` for a printable
key today.

- [ ] **Step 3: Add the debounce plumbing**

In `internal/tui/keys.go`, beside `clipboardMessageTTL`:

```go
// filterDebounce is how long after the last keystroke the in-progress filter
// is applied. Filter.Apply rebuilds and re-indexes a whole second snapshot —
// benchmarked at 149us/818KB/1,655 allocs on a 758-record fixture — so a
// burst of typing must cost one re-filter, not one per character. 150ms is
// below the threshold at which a pause reads as lag and above a fast typist's
// inter-key interval.
const filterDebounce = 150 * time.Millisecond
```

Add to `overlayState`:

```go
	// filterToken is the generation of the most recently scheduled filter
	// apply. A tick carrying an older one is discarded — see
	// applyBufferedFilter. Same shape as statusState.token, and for the same
	// reason: a timer that can outlive what it was scheduled for.
	filterToken int
	// filterBefore is the filter as it was when the overlay opened, which is
	// what Escape restores. It has to be remembered rather than recomputed:
	// typing applies as it goes now, so by the time Escape arrives m.filter
	// already holds the edit.
	filterBefore beads.Filter
```

And the message, beside `clearStatusMsg`:

```go
// filterTickMsg asks Update (app.go) to apply the in-progress filter text.
// token pins it to the keystroke that scheduled it, so a tick still in flight
// when another character arrives applies nothing.
type filterTickMsg struct{ token int }
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Remember the filter when the overlay opens**

In `handleActionKey`'s `Filter` case:

```go
	case key.Matches(msg, m.keys.Filter):
		m.overlay.kind, m.overlay.buffer = overlayFilter, m.filter.Text
		m.overlay.filterBefore = m.filter
		m.applyLayout(m.layout.Width, m.layout.Height)

		return nil, true
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Schedule, apply and restore**

In `internal/tui/keys.go`:

```go
// scheduleFilterApply debounces the live filter: every keystroke bumps the
// generation and schedules exactly one tick.
//
// token is captured by value here, deliberately. A closure that read
// m.overlay.filterToken when the tick fired would always see the latest
// generation, so every stale tick would report itself as current and the
// guard in applyBufferedFilter would never reject anything.
func (m *Model) scheduleFilterApply() tea.Cmd {
	m.overlay.filterToken++
	token := m.overlay.filterToken

	return tea.Tick(filterDebounce, func(time.Time) tea.Msg {
		return filterTickMsg{token: token}
	})
}

// applyBufferedFilter applies the in-progress text, but only for the tick the
// most recent keystroke scheduled, and only while the overlay is still open.
// The second guard is what makes a tick that outlived Escape harmless: by
// then the previous filter has already been restored, and re-applying the
// abandoned buffer over it would undo that silently, a frame later.
func (m *Model) applyBufferedFilter(token int) {
	if token != m.overlay.filterToken || m.overlay.kind != overlayFilter {
		return
	}

	filter := m.filter
	filter.Text = m.overlay.buffer
	m.SetFilter(filter)
}
```

Rewrite `handleFilterKey`'s body — Enter unchanged, Escape restoring, both
editing branches scheduling:

```go
	switch msg.Code {
	case tea.KeyEnter:
		filter := m.filter
		filter.Text = m.overlay.buffer
		m.SetFilter(filter)
		m.closeFilterOverlay()
	case tea.KeyEscape:
		// Restore, not clear. Typing applies as it goes now, so m.filter
		// already holds the abandoned edit; filterBefore is the only record
		// of what the user had before opening the box.
		m.SetFilter(m.overlay.filterBefore)
		m.closeFilterOverlay()
	case tea.KeyBackspace:
		if n := len(m.overlay.buffer); n > 0 {
			m.overlay.buffer = m.overlay.buffer[:n-1]
		}

		return m.scheduleFilterApply()
	default:
		if msg.Text != "" {
			m.overlay.buffer += msg.Text

			return m.scheduleFilterApply()
		}
	}

	return nil
```

```go
// closeFilterOverlay clears the overlay and gives the body back the row the
// filter line was using. Enter and Escape differ only in which filter they
// leave behind, so the teardown is shared.
func (m *Model) closeFilterOverlay() {
	m.overlay.kind, m.overlay.buffer = overlayNone, ""
	m.applyLayout(m.layout.Width, m.layout.Height)
}
```

Leave the byte-slicing backspace exactly as it is. It mishandles multi-byte
input, and that is a pre-existing bug worth its own ticket — fixing it here
would bury it inside an unrelated commit.

- [ ] **Step 6: Route the tick**

In `internal/tui/app.go`'s `Update`, beside the `clearStatusMsg` case:

```go
		m.applyBufferedFilter(msg.token)

		return m, nil
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Stage, run the gate, and commit**

```bash

        internal/tui/app_test.go internal/tui/export_test.go
task check
git commit -m "feat(tui): apply the filter as you type, and restore on escape

Every keystroke schedules one tick 150ms out carrying the generation that
scheduled it, so a burst of typing costs one re-filter rather than one per

Escape now restores the filter as it was when the box opened rather than
discarding an edit that has already been applied — including when the box
was opened on an already-active filter, where clearing would lose a query
the user never touched. A tick that outlives the overlay is dropped by the
same guard."
```

title: Blockedness does not propagate down parent-child edges
description:
internal/beads under-reports blocked issues: br treats a child of a blocked parent as itself blocked, and bv does not.

Symptom: TestMatchesBrBlocked (internal/beads/derive_test.go:177) fails against this repository's own .beads/ workspace. br blocked reports bv-f7b.2.1 with blocked_by [bv-f7b.2]; bv's Snapshot.IsBlocked reports it unblocked.

Repro: an issue whose own blocks-dependencies are all closed or absent, whose parent is reachable in the snapshot, and whose parent is itself blocked. bv-f7b.2.1 is the live case: its only blocks-dep (bv-f7b.1.2) is closed, its parent bv-f7b.2 is open and blocked by bv-f7b.1.

Expected: bv agrees with br — a non-terminal issue is blocked when its parent is blocked, transitively up the parent chain.

Evidence this is propagation and not simply 'an open parent blocks': bv-f7b.3.1's parent bv-f7b.3 is open but carries no blocking dependency, and br does NOT report bv-f7b.3.1 as blocked. Only children of *blocked* parents are listed.

derive.go's IsBlocked comment claims to mirror br's blocker query exactly and states that parent-child edges do not block. That remains true for the direct edge; what is missing is the separate inherited rule. Any fix must keep the existing two rules intact (a dependency on an id absent from the snapshot still blocks; an epic with an open non-template child is blocked) and must not recurse without cycle protection — hand-edited JSONL can contain a parent cycle.

design:
# Tree row parity and board column navigation

Two changes from a read-through of the finished interface work: the tree's
rows never gained the colour and the date column the list rows did, and the
board's cursor still parks on columns that hold nothing.

## Global constraint

Non-test Go stands at **6,952 against a ceiling of 7,000** — 48 lines of
headroom. The extraction below is close to net-neutral (code leaves
`listview` as it arrives in `rowfmt`), and the two features are estimated at
roughly +40 lines, so this is expected to fit. It is tight.

**If it does not fit, raise the ceiling and say so in that commit.** Do not
compress comments to land on the number. The previous epic did exactly that
once and lost the meaning of a paragraph that had to be restored in a later
pass; the cap is a proxy for structural regression, not a target.

## Architecture

`internal/tui/listview` currently owns the row composer — `rowColumns`,
`compose`, `fitAge`, `fitTitleAndLabels`, `plain`, `styled`, `pad` — all
unexported. The tree needs the same machinery, and for the same non-obvious
reason: a row cannot be styled uniformly and per-column at once, because a
per-column foreground inside `theme.Selected`'s background emits a reset that
drops that background for the rest of the line.

Copying it into `treeview` would leave two implementations of a rule that
took a fix round to get right the first time. So it moves to a new package,
`internal/tui/rowfmt`, consumed by both views. The two view packages stay
independent of one another; neither imports the other.

`rowfmt` owns composition and styling. It does **not** own the width ladder —
which column is sacrificed first differs between the views, and that decision
stays with each view.

## Features

### F1 — Tree rows reach list parity

Tree rows today are `prefix + glyph + id + priority + title`, rendered under a
single style chosen from three: `Selected`, `Muted` for an ancestor retained
only to keep a matching descendant reachable, and `Base` otherwise.

They gain what the list rows have: the type glyph coloured by issue type, the
priority by level, a status column coloured by status, and the right-aligned
relative age column. Selection stays a single highlight; the muted-ancestor
path stays muted as a whole, since that mutedness is a statement about the
row rather than about any one column.

The width ladder extends rather than changes. The tree's prefix grows with
depth, so the title — the only column that identifies the row — is what must
survive. In order of sacrifice: **age, then status, then id, then the title
truncates.** The existing `fitTitle`/`minTitleWidth` floor keeps its meaning.

Acceptance criteria:
- A tree row renders its glyph, priority and status each in its own style,
  and carries a right-aligned relative age.
- A selected row renders as one highlight with no style gap across the row.
- A non-matching retained ancestor still renders muted as a whole.
- As width falls, the columns drop in the order above; at every width the
  rendered line fits, and the title is present whenever anything after the
  prefix is.
- At a depth where the prefix alone approaches the pane width, the row
  degrades rather than panicking — the existing final truncate still applies.
- Golden frames regenerated and read.

### F2 — The board's cursor skips empty columns

`MoveLeft` and `MoveRight` step one column at a time and stop wherever they
land, including on a column with no issues. `clamp` then keeps the column
selected with no issue under the cursor, which empties the detail pane and
leaves the two movement keys doing something that looks like nothing.

The code's own justification for that — "an unreachable column hides the fact
that it is empty" — no longer holds: `columnHeaderLines` renders every
column's title, `(0)` count and stats line whether or not the cursor is on it,
so an empty column is visible on screen regardless. Since `c` became a global
hide-closed toggle, empty columns are also far more common than they were.

`MoveLeft` and `MoveRight` now move to the nearest column **in that direction
that holds at least one issue**, and stop where they are when there is none.
When every column is empty the cursor does not move at all.

`clamp` keeps its current behaviour unchanged — it is what makes a column
reachable at all after a regrouping, and a board whose only populated column
disappears on reload must still land somewhere valid.

Acceptance criteria:
- Right from a populated column with one empty column beside it lands two
  columns over, on the next populated one.
- Right with no populated column to the right leaves the cursor where it was.
- The same both ways for left.
- A board whose columns are all empty does not move and does not panic.
- Empty columns still render, with their header, count and stats.
- `home`/`end`, swimlane cycling and card expansion are unaffected.
- A regrouping or reload that empties the cursor's column still leaves the
  cursor somewhere valid, via `clamp`.

## Testing

Every package keeps its single `Test<Package>` entry point wiring suites, with
all assertions as suite methods. Golden view tests store ANSI-stripped frames
and assert styling separately.

Both features carry a documented trap from the previous epic: a test that
passes while the thing it pins is broken. For F1, a test asserting only that a
row emits more than one escape sequence does not pin per-column colour — the
mutation to check is collapsing the row to a single render. For F2, a test
whose fixture has no empty column between two populated ones cannot fail if
skipping is removed.

## Out of scope

Hiding empty columns, changing `clamp`, adding a status or age column to the
board's cards, and any change to how the list composes its own rows beyond
moving the shared code. `bv` stays read-only with respect to `.beads/` and
still spawns no subprocess.
acceptance_criteria: Tree rows render glyph, priority and status each in their own style plus a right-aligned relative age, degrading age -> status -> id -> title as width falls; a selected row is one unbroken highlight and a retained non-matching ancestor is still muted as a whole. Board left/right land only on columns holding at least one issue, stay put when there is none in that direction, and do not move or panic when every column is empty; empty columns still render with header, count and stats. The row composer has exactly one implementation, in internal/tui/rowfmt, imported by both views and by neither view from the other. task check exits 0; any ceiling raise is deliberate and named in its commit rather than paid for by compressing comments.

# Global Constraints

Every task below implicitly includes this section. Values are copied verbatim
from CLAUDE.md and `.golangci.yml`; do not restate them per task, and do not
relax one to make a task fit.

## The gate

- `task check` runs `format:check` → `lint` → `test` and must exit 0 before
  every commit.
- Run it again **after** `git add`, not only before. The `internal/licensing`
  sweep enumerates git-tracked files, so a new file that is not yet staged is
  invisible to it: stage first, then run the gate, then commit.
- Never pass `--no-verify`. Do not skip hooks.
- Do not run `git push` or `gh` in this repository — it has no remote.

## Size tripwires

- Non-test Go: at most **7,000 lines**, and the tree stands at **6,952**.
  The extraction in the first task does not fit: moving 50 lines into a new
  package costs roughly 25 more in package declaration, doc and imports, the
  tree's ladder adds about 30, and the board about 20 — approximately +75,
  landing near 7,027. **The first task raises the ceiling to 7,100**, once,
  for this epic, with the arithmetic in its commit message.
  Do **not** land on the number by compressing comments. The previous epic
  did exactly that and lost the meaning of a paragraph that a later pass had
  to restore. The cap is a proxy for structural regression, not a target.
- `cmd/bv/main.go`: at most 150 lines.
- No non-test source file exceeds 500 lines. Test files that map to exactly one
  `suite.Suite` are exempt from the line cap.
- No behavioural type has more than 20 fields. `beads.Issue` is exempt.
- At most 5 exported type declarations per file (`revive` `max-public-structs`).
- `tui.Model` is capped at 12 fields by `TestModelStaysSmall` and is **full**.
  New root state rides on `statusState` or `overlayState`, the two structs
  sanctioned to grow.
- Never add a `//nolint` that turns out to be unnecessary — `nolintlint` fails
  the build on an unused directive.

## Code style

- No package-level `var`, no `init()` (`gochecknoglobals` / `gochecknoinits`).
- `funcorder`: exported methods before unexported; constructors first.
- `revive` function-length: at most 40 statements / 60 lines (non-test).
- `gocyclo` / `cyclop`: cyclomatic complexity at most 10.
- `lll` / `golines`: 120 columns (non-test).
- `wrapcheck`: wrap every error crossing a package boundary,
  e.g. `fmt.Errorf("decode issues.jsonl: %w", err)`.
- `ireturn`: return concrete types, not interfaces. Accepting interfaces is fine.
- `sloglint`: `no-global: all`, lowercased messages, snake_case keys.
- `godot`: comments end with a period.
- Formatters: `gofumpt`, `gci` (sections: standard, default,
  `prefix(github.com/Toshik1978/beads-viewer)`), `golines` at 120 columns.
- `revive`'s `flag-parameter` rule is **disabled** in this repository, so a
  `focused bool` parameter is allowed — `Compute(width, height int, showDetail
  bool)` already relies on that.
- Write comments that explain *why*, not what the code already says.

## Dependencies

- At most 9 direct dependencies. **No task here adds one.** Everything needed
  is already present: `charm.land/bubbletea/v2`, `charm.land/bubbles/v2`,
  `charm.land/lipgloss/v2`, `charm.land/glamour/v2`,
  `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi`, `github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify`,
  `github.com/spf13/cobra`, `github.com/goccy/go-yaml`,
  `github.com/stretchr/testify`.
- Only bubbletea, bubbles, lipgloss and glamour use the `charm.land` vanity
  path; the `x/` repositories stay at `github.com/charmbracelet/x/...`.

## Testing

- Exactly one top-level `func Test<Package>(t *testing.T)` per package, wiring
  suites only — `suite.Run(t, new(...))` calls and nothing else.
- Every assertion is a suite method (`s.Equal`, `s.Require().NoError`,
  `s.Contains`). Never a bare `func TestX(t *testing.T)` with `require.X(t, …)`.
- Table-driven subtests use `s.Run(tc.name, func() { … })`.
- Golden view tests store the **ANSI-stripped** frame (`ansi.Strip`).
  Regenerate with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./...`. Styling is asserted
  separately from content — at minimum that a selected row's rendering differs
  from an unselected one.

## Behavioural invariants

- `bv` is read-only with respect to `.beads/`: it never writes anywhere inside
  that directory and never spawns a subprocess. No package under this module
  other than `internal/licensing` may import `os/exec`.
- The write to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/bv/trees/` is outside `.beads/` and is expected
  — do not "fix" it by removing it.
- `bv` renders rather than validates: unknown `status` and `issue_type` values
  stay raw strings, unknown JSON fields are ignored, labels are never
  validated. A workspace `br` itself would reject must still open.

## Commits

- Conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `test:`, `chore:`, `docs:`,
  `refactor:`.
- **No `Co-Authored-By`, no `Claude-Session`, no AI-attribution trailer of any
  kind.** Subject and body only.
- Feature branches use the `feature/` prefix — never `feat/` or `feat-`.

## Licensing

- Never name another project, or anyone else's filesystem path, in any
  git-tracked file. This applies to code, comments, commit messages and test
  fixtures alike.

### Task 3: The board's cursor skips empty columns

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/tui/boardview/boardview.go` (`MoveLeft`, `MoveRight`, plus
  one new unexported helper)
- Test: `internal/tui/boardview/boardview_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `m.columns`, `m.col`, `m.clamp()`, `m.syncSelected()`, all
  existing.
- Produces: `func (m *Model) nextPopulated(from, step int) int` — the index of
  the nearest column in direction `step` holding at least one issue, or
  `from` when there is none.

Independent of Tasks 1 and 2; it touches no shared code.

**Why this changes.** `clamp`'s doc comment justifies landing on empty columns
with "an unreachable column hides the fact that it is empty". That no longer
holds: `columnHeaderLines` (`card.go`) renders every column's title, `(0)`
count and stats line whether or not the cursor is on it, so an empty column is
on screen regardless. Since `c` became a global hide-closed toggle, empty
columns are also far more common than when that comment was written. Update
the comment as part of this task — leaving a justification standing for
behaviour that no longer exists is worse than the behaviour was.

**What must not change.** `clamp` itself. It is what makes a column reachable
at all after a regrouping, and a board whose only populated column disappears
on reload must still land somewhere valid. `nextPopulated` is a movement
concern; `clamp` is a validity concern, and conflating them would mean a
reload could strand the cursor with nothing selected and no way back.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests**

Add to `boardTestSuite`. Its constructor is `s.model(issues, w, h)` and its
fixture is `s.sample()`; add a fixture with a deliberate gap rather than
reusing `sample()`, since a board with no empty column between two populated
ones cannot fail if skipping is removed:

```go
// gapped puts an empty column between two populated ones under the status
// lane, which is the shape the skip exists for — a fixture without the gap
// passes whether or not MoveRight skips anything.
func (s *boardTestSuite) gapped() []beads.Issue {
	return []beads.Issue{
		{ID: "bv-1", Title: "open one", Status: beads.StatusOpen},
		{ID: "bv-2", Title: "blocked one", Status: beads.StatusBlocked},
	}
}

func (s *boardTestSuite) TestRightSkipsAnEmptyColumn() {
	m := s.model(s.gapped(), 200, 20)
	s.Require().Equal("bv-1", m.SelectedID())

	before := s.columnIndexOf(m, "bv-1")
	m.MoveRight()

	s.Equal("bv-2", m.SelectedID(),
		"the cursor must land on the next column that holds something")
	s.Greater(s.columnIndexOf(m, "bv-2"), before+1,
		"fixture assumption: at least one empty column sat between them")
}

func (s *boardTestSuite) TestLeftSkipsAnEmptyColumn() {
	m := s.model(s.gapped(), 200, 20)
	s.Require().True(m.SelectByID("bv-2"))

	m.MoveLeft()

	s.Equal("bv-1", m.SelectedID())
}

func (s *boardTestSuite) TestMovingPastTheLastPopulatedColumnStaysPut() {
	m := s.model(s.gapped(), 200, 20)
	s.Require().True(m.SelectByID("bv-2"))

	for range 5 {
		m.MoveRight()
	}

	s.Equal("bv-2", m.SelectedID(),
		"with nothing populated to the right, the cursor does not move")
}

func (s *boardTestSuite) TestAnAllEmptyBoardDoesNotMoveOrPanic() {
	m := s.model(nil, 200, 20)

	s.NotPanics(func() {
		m.MoveRight()
		m.MoveLeft()
	})
	s.Empty(m.SelectedID())
}

func (s *boardTestSuite) TestEmptyColumnsStillRender() {
	out := ansi.Strip(s.model(s.gapped(), 200, 20).View())

	// Skipping is a navigation rule, not a visibility one: a status with
	// nothing in it is worth seeing on a board used for triage.
	s.Contains(out, "(0)")
}
```

`s.columnIndexOf` is a helper you add if the suite has no equivalent — it
finds which column holds an id. If the suite already exposes the cursor's
column, use that instead.

- [ ] **Step 2: Run them to verify they fail**

Run: `go test ./internal/tui/boardview/ -run TestBoardview`

Expected: `TestRightSkipsAnEmptyColumn` FAILs — `MoveRight` lands on the empty
column and `SelectedID` comes back `""`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the skip**

In `internal/tui/boardview/boardview.go`:

```go
// MoveLeft moves the cursor to the nearest column to the left that holds at
// least one issue, and stays where it is when there is none. Empty columns
// are skipped rather than hidden: they still render with their header, count
// and stats, so nothing about the board is concealed — the cursor simply does
// not park where there is nothing to act on.
func (m *Model) MoveLeft() {
	m.col = m.nextPopulated(m.col, -1)
	m.clamp()
	m.syncSelected()
}

// MoveRight is MoveLeft's mirror; see it for why empty columns are skipped.
func (m *Model) MoveRight() {
	m.col = m.nextPopulated(m.col, 1)
	m.clamp()
	m.syncSelected()
}

// nextPopulated returns the index of the nearest column in direction step
// that holds at least one issue, or from when there is none — including when
// every column is empty, which is why the caller can treat the result as
// always valid.
//
// This is a movement rule only. clamp stays responsible for confining the
// cursor to a cell that exists, because a regrouping or a reload can empty
// the column the cursor is already on, and that case must still resolve to
// somewhere valid rather than to wherever movement last left it.
func (m *Model) nextPopulated(from, step int) int {
	for i := from + step; i >= 0 && i < len(m.columns); i += step {
		if len(m.columns[i].Issues) > 0 {
			return i
		}
	}

	return from
}
```

Then update `clamp`'s doc comment: the sentence beginning "An empty column
keeps the column selection with row 0 and no selected issue, rather than
being skipped — an unreachable column hides the fact that it is empty" is no
longer the rule. Replace it with what is now true — `clamp` still resolves an
empty column to row 0 with nothing selected, because a regrouping can leave
the cursor there, but movement no longer takes the user there deliberately.

Check whether `MoveLeft`/`MoveRight`'s callers in `keyActions` need anything:
they should not, since the signatures are unchanged.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests to verify they pass**

Run: `go test ./internal/tui/boardview/ -run TestBoardview`

Expected: PASS. These existing tests cover behaviour this task must not
break, and must still pass:
- `TestNavigationIsTotal` — the 500-move fuzz over a multi-column board
- `TestMovingIntoAShorterColumnClampsTheRow`
- `TestEmptyColumnIsReachableAndSelectsNothing` — **this one pins exactly the
  behaviour being removed.** Do not delete it silently: rewrite it to assert
  what is now true (an empty column renders and is *not* landed on by
  movement, while `clamp` still resolves to it safely after a regrouping), or
  replace it with a test of `clamp`'s own contract. Say which you chose.
- `TestCycleSwimLanePreservesSelection`

- [ ] **Step 5: Verify the test can fail**

Revert `MoveRight` to `m.col++` and confirm `TestRightSkipsAnEmptyColumn`
fails. Restore it. Report what failed — a fixture without a real gap would
have passed either way, which is the trap this step exists to rule out.

- [ ] **Step 6: Stage, run the gate, and commit**

```bash
git add internal/tui/boardview/ && task check
git commit -m "feat(board): skip empty columns when moving left or right

The cursor now lands only on columns that hold something. Empty columns
still render with their header, count and stats — skipping is a navigation
rule, not a visibility one, and a status with nothing in it is worth seeing
on a board used for triage.

clamp is unchanged and still resolves an empty column safely: a regrouping
or a reload can leave the cursor on one, and that has to stay valid. What
changed is only that movement no longer takes the user there deliberately.

The old behaviour was justified by an unreachable column hiding that it was
empty. columnHeaderLines renders every column regardless, so that was
already untrue, and a global hide-closed toggle made empty columns common."
```
acceptance_criteria: Right and left each land on the next populated column across a real gap, verified with a fixture that has an empty column between two populated ones; movement past the last populated column in either direction leaves the cursor where it was; an all-empty board neither moves nor panics; empty columns still render with header, count and stats; clamp's behaviour and doc are updated rather than left asserting a removed rule; TestEmptyColumnIsReachableAndSelectsNothing is rewritten rather than deleted silently; reverting MoveRight to m.col++ fails a test, verified by performing that mutation; TestNavigationIsTotal still passes; task check exits 0.

design:
# Hide-closed by default, selection that follows the view, and a dependency board

Three changes to how `bv` presents a workspace, driven by three complaints from
daily use: closed issues are noise until you ask for them, switching views loses
your place, and answering "what is holding this up, and what is waiting on it"
means reading the detail pane rather than seeing it.

## Architecture

Nothing about the layering changes. `beads.Filter` is still applied exactly once,
in `Model.applyFilter`, and the identical filtered snapshot still reaches every
view. The views stay peers behind the `View` interface, and the root `Model`
stays at its 12-field cap: the dependency view is a fourth array slot and a
fourth package, not four new fields.

Two structural additions carry the third feature:

- `beads.Snapshot` gains a reverse dependency index, built in the same single
  pass that already builds `children`, `parentOf` and `roots`. Today the only
  way to answer "what does this issue block" is a linear scan over every issue,
  which `detail.renderBlocks` performs on every render.
- Card rendering moves out of `boardview` into a new shared package,
  `internal/tui/cardfmt`, exactly as `rowfmt` was extracted for the row logic
  the list and tree share. Without it the dependency view would either duplicate
  the card or import `boardview`, and "views are peers, they do not import each
  other" would be broken by the fourth view the way it was nearly broken by the
  third.

## Tech Stack

Unchanged. No new dependency: the dependency view is built from
`charm.land/lipgloss/v2` and `charm.land/bubbletea/v2`, both already direct
dependencies, and the reverse index is plain maps in `internal/beads`.

---

## Feature 1 — Hide closed by default

`config.Load`'s built-in default becomes:

```go
cfg := Config{Theme: ThemeAuto, View: ViewList, HideClosed: true}
```

That is the whole behavioural change. "On all views" needs no work, because one
filter already feeds all of them.

The ways back are the ones that already exist, and no new flag is added: a second
positive spelling would mean two flags for one boolean and a precedence rule
nobody wants to reason about.

- `--hide-closed=false`
- `hide_closed: false` in `~/.config/bv/config.yaml`
- `BV_HIDE_CLOSED=false`
- `c` at runtime

The status bar keeps announcing the narrowing. `Filter.IsZero()` is false at the
new default, so `renderStatus` emits `list (12 hidden) | hide closed` on every
frame, exactly as it does today once `c` is pressed. This is deliberate: the
hidden count is the only honest signal that issues are missing, and the filter
segment is what makes `c` discoverable. No code in `status.go` changes.

Tombstones remain hidden independently of this toggle, and `Model.statusLine`'s
existing `Counts.Closed - Counts.Tombstones` subtraction already keeps the hidden
count from reporting issues hide-closed did not hide.

### Acceptance criteria

- A `bv` started with no flags, no environment and no config file opens with
  terminal-status issues hidden in the list, the tree and the board.
- `--hide-closed=false`, `hide_closed: false` and `BV_HIDE_CLOSED=false` each
  restore the previous behaviour, and the existing precedence order between them
  is unchanged.
- `HideClosedSet` still distinguishes an absent flag from `--hide-closed=false`,
  so an unset flag cannot override a config file.
- The status bar reads the hidden count and the `hide closed` filter segment at
  the default, with no keypress.
- README's flags table, config example and hide-closed section state the new
  default.

---

## Feature 2 — Every view opens on the active item

Switching views currently only assigns `Model.active`. Each view keeps its own
cursor, so the tree lands wherever it was last left — row 0 on a fresh run, or a
row restored from `$XDG_STATE_HOME/bv/trees/`. This is not a scrolling defect:
`treeview.ensureCursorVisible` and `bubbles/v2/list`'s own `Select` (which sets
`Paginator.Page`) both position their viewport correctly. The selection simply
was never carried across.

`handleViewSwitchKey` reads the outgoing view's `Selected()` before switching and
asks the incoming view to reveal that id. That requires one new method on the
`View` interface:

```go
Reveal(id string) bool
```

- `listview` and `boardview` already have exactly this behaviour under the name
  `SelectByID`, which keeps its name and its existing callers —
  `Model.openSelectedInList` and `boardview`'s own tests. `Reveal` is a
  one-line method delegating to it, not a rename.
- `treeview` needs new work. Its `SelectByID` searches flattened rows only, so it
  fails whenever the target sits inside a collapsed subtree. `Reveal` walks the
  parent chain with `Snapshot.Parent`, sets `Expanded` on each ancestor, records
  each through `rememberExpanded`, then calls `refreshRows` and positions the
  cursor.
- `depsview` (Feature 5) implements `Reveal` by re-rooting rather than by moving
  a cursor, so it succeeds for any id present in the filtered snapshot.

Revealing in the tree therefore mutates `expandedIDs`, which is persisted on
exit. This is accepted rather than worked around: the walk only ever expands,
never collapses, so the worst outcome is a tree that reopens wider than it was
left — strictly better than one that reopens with the issue you were looking at
hidden.

The board's `enter` binding becomes a special case of this rule and stays as it
is.

### Acceptance criteria

- Selecting an issue in the list and pressing `2` puts the tree's cursor on that
  issue, expanding every ancestor needed to make its row exist, with the viewport
  scrolled so the row is on screen.
- The same holds for every other ordered pair of views, in both directions.
- An id the incoming view cannot resolve (filtered out) leaves that view's cursor
  where it was, and the switch still happens.
- A tree reveal never collapses a node the user had expanded.
- Switching views still returns focus to the view rather than leaving it on the
  detail pane.

---

## Feature 3 — Reverse dependency index

`beads.Snapshot` answers "what blocks this issue" through `Blockers`, but has no
index for the reverse. `detail.renderBlocks` compensates by scanning
`Snapshot.Issues()` on every render, and the dependency view would need the same
answer far more often.

`indexHierarchy` already walks every issue's `Dependencies` once. That walk gains
a second map, keyed by the depended-on id, and two accessors:

- `Dependents(id) []*Issue` — issues declaring a blocking edge on `id`, in
  canonical order.
- `RelatedTo(id) []*Issue` — issues joined to `id` by a `related` or
  `discovered-from` edge in either direction, deduplicated.

Both clone on the way out, as every other snapshot accessor does. Both must
honour `NewSnapshot`'s duplicate-id policy the way `Parent` does: an index keyed
by id can only report one answer per id, so it records the edge only for the
record `byID` actually resolves to.

`detail.renderBlocks` moves onto `Dependents` and stops scanning.

### Acceptance criteria

- `Dependents` returns exactly the issues whose own `Dependencies` hold an edge
  of a blocking type pointing at the id, and nothing else.
- `RelatedTo` returns both directions of a `related` edge and both directions of
  a `discovered-from` edge, with no issue appearing twice and the subject itself
  never appearing.
- Both return a nil or empty slice for an unknown id rather than panicking.
- Both clone, so a caller mutating the result cannot corrupt the snapshot.
- `detail.renderBlocks` produces byte-identical output to its scanning
  predecessor across the existing golden fixtures.

---

## Feature 4 — Extract card rendering into `internal/tui/cardfmt`

`boardview/card.go` holds the card renderer and its content helpers alongside
board-specific chrome. The card is what the dependency view needs; the chrome is
not.

Moves to `cardfmt`:

- `renderCard` and `cardHeight`, exported
- `cardContentLines`, `headerLine`, `assigneeLine`, `blockedByLine`
- `minCardContentWidth`, `cardBorderRows`, `collapsedLines`, `expandedExtraLines`

Stays in `boardview`:

- `columnHeaderLines`, `renderMarker`, `moreLabel`, `CatchallMarker` — all of
  which are about columns, statistics and the board's own horizontal scroll
  window, none of which the dependency view has.

The package must stay under the five-exported-type limit and must not acquire a
width ladder of its own, for the same reason `rowfmt` does not own one: which
column a view sacrifices first differs per view, and only the shared parts
belong in a shared package.

### Acceptance criteria

- `boardview`'s rendered output is unchanged, pinned by its existing golden
  tests.
- `cardfmt` imports no view package, and no view package imports another.
- `cardfmt` declares at most five exported types.
- `boardview/card.go` and the new `cardfmt` package each stay under 500 lines.

---

## Feature 5 — The dependency view

A fourth peer view in a new package, `internal/tui/depsview`, reached with `4` and
selectable as `--view deps`, `view: deps` or `BV_VIEW=deps`. It renders full
screen, as the board does: `showsDetail()` excludes it, because squeezing four
columns into 42% of the terminal to describe one card is the trade that method
already refuses for the board.

### Columns

Left to right, each rendered with `cardfmt`'s card:

| Column | Contents |
|---|---|
| `blocked by (N)` | `Snapshot.Blockers`; each `DanglingBlockers` id as a card marked as absent from the workspace; the `BlockedAncestor` result tagged as inherited; and, when `BlockedByOpenChild` is true, the open children |
| `focused` | A single card: the issue the view is currently rooted on |
| `blocks (N)` | `Snapshot.Dependents` |
| `related (N)` | `Snapshot.RelatedTo`, each card tagged with the edge kind that produced it |

Parent and child edges are deliberately absent: that hierarchy is the tree view's
subject, and repeating it here would make the left and right columns mean two
things at once.

The left column's four sources are all answers to "what is holding this up", and
`Snapshot` already exposes each separately precisely so a caller can name which
applies without re-deriving any of them. An empty `Blockers` result does not mean
unblocked, which is why all four are asked.

### Navigation

The board's vocabulary, so nothing new has to be learnt:

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `left` / `h`, `right` / `l` | move between columns, skipping empty ones |
| `up` / `k`, `down` / `j` | move within a column |
| `home` / `g`, `end` / `G` | first and last card in the column |
| `enter` | re-root the view on the highlighted card |
| `backspace` | return to the previously focused issue |

`enter` pushes the outgoing focus onto a history stack that `backspace` pops, so
walking down a chain of blockers and coming back does not lose the path. The
stack lives on `depsview.Model`, not on the root model.

Entering the view with `4` roots it on whatever the previous view had selected —
this is `Reveal` from Feature 2, with the dependency view's implementation
re-rooting rather than moving a cursor. Leaving with `1`, `2` or `3` carries the
currently focused id out through the same mechanism, so a walk performed here
lands the list or tree on where it ended.

### Filtering

Columns are built from the filtered snapshot, because filtering happens once and
no view filters for itself. With hide-closed on by default, a closed blocker
therefore does not appear in the left column, which is correct: a closed blocker
is a satisfied one and `Snapshot.blocks` already treats it as such.

If the active filter excludes the focused issue itself, the view falls back the
way `boardview.regroup` does — reconciling against what survives rather than
rendering a root that is no longer there.

### Acceptance criteria

- Pressing `4` from any view opens the dependency view rooted on that view's
  selected issue.
- The left column names every reason `Snapshot.IsBlocked` would return true,
  including a dangling id, an inherited ancestor and an epic's open children,
  each visibly distinguished from a plain blocker.
- The right column lists exactly `Dependents`, and the fourth column exactly
  `RelatedTo` with edge kinds shown.
- `enter` on a card in any column re-roots the view on that card, and
  `backspace` returns to the previous root; repeated `backspace` walks the whole
  chain back and then does nothing.
- Column movement skips empty columns and never parks the cursor on a cell that
  does not exist.
- The view never renders a line wider than its allotted width, at any terminal
  size including degenerate ones.
- `depsview` exposes `HelpKeys()` so `help_test.go`'s two-way comparison covers
  it.
- A golden test stores the ANSI-stripped frame, and styling is asserted
  separately — at minimum that a selected card renders differently from an
  unselected one.

---
